reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (ranked pregame, taskId pregame-found-countdown-reduced; phone evidence in docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/loop-3.json fixcheck 'K2-first-game-GO' and appBugs):
1) MAJOR regression from round loop-2's warm-up (apps/mobile/src/screens/match/warmGame.ts, see docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/fix-loop2.json pregame item K2): in the FIRST ranked game after launch, only the tap sound and 2 countdown beats play — the matchFound chime, the '3' beat and the GO sound are missing (dumpsys audio shows 3 starts against 5 in later games). Find why players built by the warm-up during the search (or built while another is loading) don't play their first time (expo-audio player not loaded yet when play() is called → dropped? replace/seekTo race? the warm-up creating a second player for the same cue? preloadCues and the cue's own lazy creation racing?). Fix so every cue plays in the first game, keeping GO!→board at ~1.0-1.1 s. Test with the sfx/expo-audio mocks: a cue whose player was created but isn't loaded yet must still play once loaded (or be played via a path that waits).
2) minor: once in 12 recordings, ~250 ms of empty screen (only the ambient background, no GO!, no header, no board) between GO! and the board; once a single empty 50 ms frame between the search radar and the VS. Find the gap in the GO!→board / search→VS handoff (one view unmounts before the next is drawn) and overlap them (the next screen mounted under the old one before the old fades), respecting Reduced Motion.

items.id: 1 (MAJOR) pregame-found-countdown-reduced: in the first ranked game the matchFound chime, the '3' beat and the GO sound don't play
items.rootCause: The cause is in how sfx plays a player it made ahead of time on Android. The warm-up itself is fine. QA's dumpsys logs (rec/RF8Y30L038L-g6.aud and g7.aud) show it. The warm-up's players open their AudioTrack the moment they are made (03:51:57.6–58.0, sessions 3225 = matchFound, 3241 = countdownBeat, 3257 = go). After that, every play that works shows 'releasing old piid, new piid, started', which means the track was flushed by a real seek. On its first play, a player that sat idle for a few seconds shows no event at all. Here is why. While paused, ExoPlayer (media3 1.9) hands the whole short clip to the track and stops it at the end of the stream, so after a moment the player counts the clip as already played. sfx.play() then calls seekTo(0) and play(). seekTo(0) on a READY player that is already at 0 ms is skipped by ExoPlayer (same position), so nothing clears that state, and play() ends the clip at once with no sound. The second play seeks back from ENDED, which is a real seek, so it works. That is why beats '2' and '1' played and '3' didn't, why matchFound and go never played in game 1 but did in game 2, and why the player made lazily inside play() (the code before the warm-up) always worked. The same bug already hit the ui_tap player made on Home (no start for the first 'שחק' tap in the g6 log; the first start is the later 'מצא יריב') and every GAME_CUES player made when GameScreen mounts (e.g. the first 'correct' of a run).
items.fix: apps/mobile/src/services/sfx.ts: each player's first play now seeks to FIRST_PLAY_AT_S = 0.001 s instead of 0. Players already played are tracked in a WeakSet. A seek to 1 ms is a real seek: the track is flushed and made again, as in every play that works, whatever order seekTo and play arrive in. Every later play seeks to 0 as before. 1 ms of a 20–400 ms clip can't be heard. No timing change: the warm-up, preloading and GO!→board are untouched, so GO!→board stays ~1.0–1.1 s.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/services/__tests__/sfxFirstPlay.test.ts. Its expo-audio stand-in behaves like media3: a player left idle after being made counts its clip as played, a seek to the same ms while READY is skipped, and any other seek flushes the track and starts it if play is on. (1) The first ranked game: preloadCues(matchFound, countdownBeat, go), idle, then the cues found, 3, 2, 1, GO give 5 starts. On the old code (FIRST_PLAY_AT_S set to 0) it gives exactly 2, the same as dumpsys. (2) A preloaded player starts on its first play and on every later one (first seek 0.001, later seeks 0). (3) A player made lazily inside play() still starts. (4) Both voices of count_tick start. (5) A player released and made again also gets the first-play seek. 4 of the 5 tests fail on the old code. The existing sfx, feedback, warmGame, MatchScreen, ranked e2e and SoundAudition suites pass.
items.deviceCheck: Needs a new APK. Sound on (the default), reduced motion off, both phones. 1) Force-stop, launch, Settings, back, 'שחק' → '2 שחקנים' → wait 3 s on 'סוג משחק' → 'מהיר' → 'מצא יריב' on both phones at once, and play through VS, 3·2·1, GO. 2) 'adb shell dumpsys audio', PlaybackActivityMonitor, 'event:started' for the app's uid. After the 'מצא יריב' tap there should be 5 starts in this FIRST game: matchFound ~1.4 s after the tap, 3 beats ~1 s apart, GO ~1 s after the last beat (before: 3 starts). By ear: chime at the VS, a beat on 3, 2 and 1, GO. 3) Also check: the very first 'שחק' tap after launch now logs a start for ui_tap, and the first correct digit in the game sounds. 4) Repeat one more cold run and one warm game: 5 starts each. GO!→first board frame should stay ~1.3–1.4 s from GO!'s first frame (≈1.0–1.1 s from GO! at full size), the same as apk9.

items.id: 2b (minor) one empty 50 ms frame between the search radar and the VS
items.rootCause: In MatchScreen the search and the pre-game stage were separate keyed roots (<SearchView key='search'> and <View key='pregame'>). So the commit that mounted the VS also deleted the search, and FoundView's entrance (useEnter, opacity 0→1) starts at 0. The first frame after 'found' therefore had nothing on it. QA saw this once (g6 p1), but the frame sizes show it in more recordings too: g5 p3 02550 and p1 g2 02300 are ~1.9 KB, the size of an empty ambient frame.
items.fix: apps/mobile/src/screens/match/MatchScreen.tsx: the search now renders inside the pre-game stage from the start (<View key='pregame'><Layer key='search' shown>…). On 'found' the same SearchView instance stays under the VS in a hidden Layer and fades out (motion `stateChange` 240 ms; with Reduced Motion the shorter reducedFade) while the VS fades in over it, so the two cross-fade. It shows the last search model, kept in state (the model is now memoized, so the render-phase update settles in one pass). Once unseen, it gets reduce=true so its radar sweep and seat pulses stop. It is deleted RETIRE_MS (4 s) later, following retire.ts / docs/PERF.md B14/B32, so a view a worklet moved is never deleted while new SVG is drawn. While hidden it can't be touched (pointerEvents none) and screen readers skip it. If the match falls through and the search comes back, the same view fades back in.
items.test: New it.each in apps/mobile/src/screens/match/__tests__/MatchScreen.test.tsx, 'the VS fades in over the search, the same search view fading out under it', run with reduced motion off and on. In the commit where the VS mounts, the same 'match-search' element is still in the tree, its layer is not at opacity 0, and it is hidden from touch and screen readers. After 300 ms its layer is at opacity 0 and the radar arc is at rest (0deg). After RETIRE_MS it is gone. This fails on the old code, where 'match-search' was deleted when found came in. All 50 MatchScreen tests pass, and so do ModesRanked, ModesAndGameType and ranked e2e.
items.deviceCheck: Needs a new APK. Both phones, reduced motion off: ranked 2 players, 'מצא יריב' on both, screenrecord, 50 ms frames from the last radar frame to the full VS. Expected: no empty dark frame. There should be 4–5 frames where the radar/search fades out while the VS fades in (and slams) over it. Repeat with in-app reduced motion on: same overlap with a plain fade, nothing moves, and no empty frame. During the VS, tapping where 'ביטול חיפוש' was does nothing, and TalkBack doesn't read the search.

items.id: 2a (minor) ~250 ms of empty screen between GO! and the board (once in 12 recordings, g2 on טלפון 3)
items.rootCause: Found from the frames, but not fixed. In rec/RF8Y30L038L-g2f, GO! is fully visible at 7700. At 7750–7900 the frames are identical ~2 KB empty frames, so the match screen vanished in one frame and did not fade. At 7950 the game screen appears with only the lead bar and the lock strip, the board comes at 8000, and the cards come after that. In normal runs (e.g. g5 p3 07800→07850) GO! is also replaced in a single frame, but the game screen's first frame lands in that same frame. So the native replace (router.replace('/game'), react-native-screens fade) removes the match screen's content at once in every run, and the 150 ms fade isn't visible in any recording. The gap appears only when the game screen's first draw comes late. In that run the game screen also drew in pieces, which looks like the content arrived over several commits or layout passes. Nothing in MatchScreen goes blank: the 'play' state always renders GO!, and the store's match stays until the route goes. The cause of the late first draw is native (screen fragment, layout and size propagation, or a busy UI or JS thread at that moment). It can't be pinned down without a systrace/perfetto capture, and adb is off-limits this round.
items.fix: No code change for this part. The fixes I could see each carry risk that can't be checked without a phone: prefetching /game during the count, which mounts the whole game screen and its BackHandler and timers under the count; presenting /game as a transparent modal and removing /match after the game is drawn, which changes iOS modal behaviour and back navigation; or drawing a GO! placeholder first in the game route and mounting GameScreen a frame later. I recommend one perfetto/systrace capture of a GO!→board handoff that shows the gap before choosing one.
items.deviceCheck: With the new APK, keep recording GO!→board at 50 ms on both phones, 6+ games, with motion on and off. If an empty run of 2 or more frames shows up again, record it again with 'adb shell perfetto' or systrace (UI thread, RenderThread, mqt_js, the gfx/view/am categories) around GO!. Then compare when the old screen's fragment is removed and when the game screen's first draw happens.

rep.notes:
Checks run: npx jest on apps/mobile/src/screens/match, apps/mobile/src/services/__tests__, ModesRanked, ModesAndGameType, ranked.e2e and SoundAuditionScreen: 25 suites, 489 tests passed. npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit is clean, eslint is clean on the 4 changed files, and prettier was run only on those files. The fix lives in sfx.play(), so it covers all of these, and staged practice (TapLevelScreen, PuzzleLevelScreen preloadCues) too.

reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (in-game layout; taskIds interference-picker-grid-small, interference-picker-opens):
1) MAJOR: on a 360x780dp screen (Settings → display zoom max = density 540 on the A16), in a 2-player game (ranked or friends room) the opponent's card at the top is cut off at the left edge: card-opponent bounds [0,114][489,654], the avatar half off-screen, the score '0' and 'חושב…' cut; my card is 537 px wide (489-1026), so the opponent card would need to start at -48. In the arsenal sheet the 'יעד' tag under the card frame shows only '…'. At 384dp all is fine. Find the 2P header layout (GameScreen / player cards) and make both cards fit any width ≥ 320dp (share width, shrink avatar/score per the design system — but never tiny text: Moshe hates tiny digits; wrap or reduce secondary info instead), with a test at 320 and 360 dp.
2) In the interference picker (apps/mobile/src/screens/game/arsenal/ArsenalOverlay.tsx TargetLine) the 2-player target row shows avatar, name and flag but NOT the player's shape (▲), though the opponent card shows it. CLAUDE.md: every player has a shape (● ▲ ■ ◆) so ownership never depends on colour alone. Add the shape to the target line in 2P like 3-4P, with the same bidi handling.

items.rootCause: At the largest display zoom the A16 is really 320 dp wide (1080 px at density 540; the tester's '360x780' is a mix-up). The 2-player cards had a fixed width of 159 (styles.card = size.playerCard.width), and DuelHud put them in a 288-dp row (320 minus the 16-dp gutters). 2 x 159 = 318, so the row overflowed by 30 dp. With RTL space-between, my card stayed at the right edge and the opponent's card started 14 dp (48 px) off the left edge, matching the reported bounds [0..489] for 537 px. That cut off its avatar, its score '0' and 'חושב…'.
items.fix: New pure helper duelCardWidth(rowWidth) in components/player/metrics.ts (exported from the index): min(159, floor((row - pairGap) / 2)), with pairGap = space[4] = 8. Every width from 360 dp up gets 159 exactly as before (at 360 the gap stays 10). At 320 each card is 140. PlayerCard takes an optional `width` prop (default 159). DuelHud measures its row with onLayout, starting from the window width minus the gutters before the first layout, passes the width to both cards, and still forwards onLayout to the screen. The score stays Teko 64 and the name Rubik 16, so no text is made tiny. The name ends in '…' a little sooner, and the status-row words use the existing B47 wrap/shrink (Hebrew fits at full size at 140). reactions/model defaultCardRect (the first-frame guess for the picker and menu) uses the same width. Added a note to docs/design/components.md §3.1.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/screens/game/__tests__/DuelHud.test.tsx. It checks that duelCardWidth keeps two cards plus the gap inside the row at every width from 320 to 430, gives 159 at 360/390 and 140 at 320. It renders DuelHud at 320 and at 360 dp and checks that both cards are equal and fit the row, and that score and name font sizes stay 64 and 16. It fires a layout event and checks the cards follow the measured row, and checks defaultCardRect. On the old code the 320 case fails (159*2+8 > 288) and duelCardWidth does not exist. Ran the related suites (components/player incl. statusFit, game/reactions, arsenal, GameScreenDuel/Faces/Online, interferenceRanked e2e, docs tests): all pass. tsc: no errors in my files (the only errors are in screens/legal/__tests__/LicensesScreen.test.tsx, another agent's file). eslint and prettier are clean.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 1 (SM-A165F), Hebrew, font size 1.0: Settings → Display → Screen zoom → largest (density 540). Cold-start the app and open a 2-player friends room or ranked match. 1) Check the cards at the top: the opponent's card (left) and mine (right) are both fully on screen. The opponent's avatar is whole and about 16 dp from the left edge, and the score '0' and 'חושב…' are whole. There are about 8 dp between the cards, and the VS badge sits between them as at normal zoom. card-opponent should start at about x=54 px. 2) Solve until you have 2 points and tap 'הפרעה': the 'יעד' chip under the opponent card's frame reads 'יעד' in full, not '…'. 3) Grid check (same task): the six kinds show in a 3x2 grid with no scrolling. 4) Return to normal zoom (384 dp): both cards are 159 dp, as before. Then restore the display zoom and navigation settings.

items.rootCause: In ArsenalOverlay.tsx, TargetLine (the 2-player header 'יעד: [avatar] name flag') drew the avatar ring in the seat colour but left out the SeatGlyph. Only the 3–4 player RouteLine drew the shapes. components.md §13 already says the 2P line includes the seat glyph (▲ ■ ◆), so this was an implementation gap and not a design choice.
items.fix: TargetLine now draws <SeatGlyph colorIndex={target.colorIndex} size={m.subtitle.glyph} /> between the ringed mini avatar and the name, the same order and size as RouteLine's RouteFace. Bidi is unchanged and matches the route: the glyph is decorative (hidden from screen readers), and the single accessible label stays t('arsenal.targetLabel', { name: isolate(name) }) with the name in FSI/PDI isolation. No new strings.
items.test: New case in apps/mobile/src/screens/game/arsenal/__tests__/ArsenalOverlay.test.tsx, '2 players: the target line has their shape too'. It opens the picker in a 2-player game and checks that arsenal-target contains glyph-triangle (the opponent's P2 shape), no glyph-circle, and the accessible name 'יעד: ⁨Mr. Hoot⁩'. It fails on the old code because there is no glyph. All 19 tests in the suite pass.
items.deviceCheck: Two phones, 2-player friends room (or ranked against the hidden bot): on phone A, solve until the score is at least 2 and tap 'הפרעה' on the opponent's card. The line under 'בחר הפרעה' reads 'יעד:', then the opponent's avatar in a ring of their colour, then ▲ in the same colour, then the name and flag, as on the opponent card. With TalkBack on, the line is read once as 'יעד: <name>' and the shape is not read. Repeat on phone 3, and in English check the order is 'Target: [avatar] ▲ name flag'.

rep.notes: The A16 at density 540 is 320 dp wide, not 360, so the fix and its test target 320. At 360 dp nothing changes: cards stay 159 with 10 dp between them, and the VS badge overlaps the cards' inner header corners a little, the same as before. At 320 each card is 140 dp. Hebrew fits at full size: the status row is at scale 1.0 and the 'חושב…'/'הפרעה' pair fits. I measured other languages with font metrics at 140 dp and they stay at about 0.75 or more, except en, ar, ru and tr: their 'הפרעה' button word would need about 0.6–0.7 and may end in '…' only at this extreme zoom (en-XA already fails at 159). I left statusFit.test (which checks 159) unchanged. Score digits are never shrunk, so a 3-digit score with its +delta (for example '188.5 +3.5', about 159 dp) can briefly overflow a 140-dp card's inner side at 320 dp. That is rare and acceptable. I could not reproduce the 'יעד' chip showing '…' in Jest. It was most likely a side effect of the card hanging off-screen, so please re-check it on the device (deviceCheck step 2). No adb, build, install, git stash/commit or i18n keys were used.

reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (taskIds stealth-play-bg-long, interference-picker-grid-small (2nd bug), account-settings-licenses-expand):
1) After 15 s in the background during a ranked game, on return the first frame (~1 s) shows the banner 'החיבור שלך אבד · מתחבר מחדש… · ניסיון 1', the 'הלוח נעול עד שתחזור' layer AND 'יש לך עוד 10 שניות לחזור · לפני שהמשחק ייחשב כנטישה', before 'חזרת למשחק · הכל סונכרן'. The user is already back: the 'N seconds to return before it counts as abandoning' countdown (meant for being away) must not show once the app is in the foreground; show only the reconnecting state. Check the spec (docs/01-SPEC.md reconnection/abandon) for the intended texts.
2) Friends room: after a game ended by surrender, force-stop + launch on the host phone → the app reopens 'חדר עם חברים' with 'משהו השתבש בשרת. נסה שוב בעוד רגע.' (logcat 'Room connection was closed unexpectedly (4002)'); 'נסה שוב' then shows 'החדר נסגר.'. A room that no longer exists / was closed must show 'החדר נסגר.' (or go Home) directly, not a server error. Also consider whether reopening a finished room at launch makes sense at all.
3) Licenses screen (apps/mobile/src/screens/legal/LicensesScreen.tsx): in the Hebrew UI the English licence texts (OFL, MIT full text, package names/versions, copyright lines) are right-aligned and the package row is in RTL order. English legal text must be LTR and left-aligned (writingDirection 'ltr', textAlign 'left' on the content; package row in LTR order), the Hebrew headings stay RTL.

items.rootCause: When the app goes to the background during an online game, RemoteGameHost deliberately closes the socket (ReconnectInfo.cause 'background') and reconnects when the app comes back. connectionStatusOf dropped `cause`, so connectionModel treated the return like a network drop and built Self-Reconnecting 'lost' with the abandonment deadline. That gave secondsLeft = 10 after 15 s away (10 s soft phase + 15 s grace), so for about 1 s the screen showed 'יש לך עוד 10 שניות לחזור · לפני שהמשחק ייחשב כנטישה' to a player who was already back.
items.fix: connectionStatus.ts now passes `cause` through on the 'reconnecting' status (a new optional field on ConnectionStatus). In connectionModel.ts, a reconnect with cause 'background' on its first attempt gives self('lost', attempt, null): secondsLeft and remainingMs are null, so LockLayer hides the countdown bar. The banner still shows 'החיבור שלך אבד · מתחבר מחדש… · ניסיון 1'. If that first try fails (attempt 2 or later, so the network really is the problem), the countdown comes back. A drop while the app is in the foreground keeps the countdown from the first try, as spec §16.2 says.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/screens/game/connection/__tests__/connectionModel.test.ts: new test 'back from the background (the first try): "reconnecting" without the abandonment countdown'. It checks secondsLeft is null on attempt 1 with cause 'background', 10 on attempt 2, and 10 for cause 'drop'. It fails on the old code. connectionStatus.test.ts now expects `cause` to be passed through.
items.deviceCheck: Phone in Hebrew. Start a quick ranked game against the stealth bot and play about a minute. Press Home, wait exactly 15 s, then return from Recents. Expected: the first frame shows only the reconnect banner ('החיבור שלך אבד · מתחבר מחדש…'), with no bottom card 'יש לך עוד N שניות לחזור / לפני שהמשחק ייחשב כנטישה'. Then 'חזרת למשחק · הכל סונכרן · המשחק ממשיך', and the game goes on. Repeat 2–3 times. Control: in a game with the app in front, turn on airplane mode for about 12 s. After the 10 s silent phase the countdown 'יש לך עוד … שניות לחזור' still appears.

items.rootCause: (2nd bug, friends room after surrender.) currentFriendsRoomCode() kept reporting the room while the session stayed connected on the results screen. A finished game is 'live', not 'closed', so followCurrentRoom kept it as the room to resume. After force-stop and launch, useAuthGate sent the app to /room/[code]?resume=1. POST /v1/rooms/join gave the player a ticket for their own seat (playsIn). But GameRoom.onJoin refused it with 'alreadyInRoom', because after the end the server holds the dropped seat for reconnection until closeAt. Colyseus sent the error and closed with 4002. friendsProblemOf maps 'alreadyInRoom' to 'internal', so the screen said 'משהו השתבש בשרת. נסה שוב בעוד רגע.'. By the time of 'נסה שוב' the room had closed, hence 'החדר נסגר.'.
items.fix: apps/mobile/src/net/friendsDevice.ts currentFriendsRoomCode() returns null once the session's game is over (session.hasGame && getView().status === 'over'), as its doc already intended ('past its game: null'). The store updates on every game update, so subscribeCurrentFriendsRoom fires at the end and followCurrentRoom calls forgetRoom(). The next launch stays on Home: reopening a finished room at launch makes no sense. A room that is still running or still in the lobby is still remembered.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/net/__tests__/friendsDevice.test.ts: new test 'past its game (still connected, on the results): no room to come back to at the next start'. It starts a friends game, checks the code is still remembered while the game runs, surrenders, then checks currentFriendsRoomCode() is null and that the subscriber got [null, FCODE, null] while the session is still not closed. It fails on the old code.
items.deviceCheck: Two phones, both signed in. Phone 1: 'צור חדר'. Phone 2 joins with the code. Start a 2-player game, then surrender on one phone (repeat once with each phone surrendering). Wait until both phones are on the results screen. Force-stop phone 1 and launch it again. Expected: the app opens on Home, not 'חדר עם חברים', and never shows 'משהו השתבש בשרת'. Control: in the lobby, before the start, force-stop phone 1 and launch it again: it still goes back to the same room.

items.rootCause: LicensesScreen's LTR style was { writingDirection: 'ltr', textAlign: 'left' }. Android ignores writingDirection. In RN 0.86 Android TextLayoutManager, the paragraph direction comes from the text's layout direction, which is RTL under forceRTL. With English (LTR) script that becomes ALIGN_OPPOSITE, which puts the text on the right. The package row (flexDirection 'row') also took the RTL layout, so the version sat left of the name.
items.fix: The LTR style now also sets the layout `direction: 'ltr'`, the pattern the repo already uses for the board, keypad and so on. That puts each English Text (names, versions, licence ids, copyright lines, the full OFL/MIT bodies) in an LTR paragraph, aligned left. The package row and its name/version line (`row`, `rowTop`) also get direction 'ltr', so the name is on the left and the version follows it. The Hebrew headings, intro and hint keep the RTL layout. A testID was added on the name/version line for the test.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/screens/legal/__tests__/LicensesScreen.test.tsx: new test 'keeps the English texts on the left in the Hebrew layout…'. It checks direction/writingDirection/textAlign LTR on the package name, version, copyright lines, font copyright and the opened OFL and MIT bodies; direction 'ltr' and flexDirection 'row' on the package row and its top line; and that the Hebrew heading 'גופנים' is not LTR. It fails on the old code.
items.deviceCheck: Hebrew UI: Home → 'הגדרות' → 'רישיונות'. Tap 'SIL Open Font License 1.1' under 'גופנים': the full text (PREAMBLE…) must be left-aligned and read left to right. Check the Rubik/Teko names and their 'Copyright …' lines are on the left. Scroll the packages: for example '@babel/code-frame' is on the left with '7.29.7' to its right, and the 'MIT' and 'Copyright (c) …' lines are on the left. Scroll to the end and tap 'MIT' under 'נוסחי הרישיונות': 'MIT License', 'Permission is hereby granted…' are left-aligned. The Hebrew headings ('גופנים', 'נוסחי הרישיונות', the intro) stay on the right, and opening and closing still work.

rep.notes:
Checks: I temporarily reverted the three source changes, and each new regression test failed on the old code (3 failed); the fixes were then restored. With the fixes, 51 related suites pass, 782 tests (connection, online, net, legal, auth, friends, ranked e2e). `npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit` passes. ESLint and Prettier pass on all changed files. No i18n keys were added; existing texts only. No server changes, adb, builds or commits.

Item 1, a design choice: the countdown is hidden only on the first reconnect attempt after a background return. The abandonment deadline is real on the server, and spec §16.2 wants the countdown for a lost connection. So if that first try fails (the network really is gone), the countdown comes back rather than letting the player be abandoned without warning. The lock card 'הלוח נעול עד שתחזור' still shows during that roughly 1 s 'lost' state, as the spec's 'locked board' requires.

Item 2, what remains (server side, not changed here): the server answers a rejoin-by-code to a seat it is still holding with 'alreadyInRoom'. That happens after the end, and also mid-game within the 25 s after the app was killed. The client shows that as 'internal' ('משהו השתבש בשרת'). With this fix a finished room is no longer resumed, so the reported flow goes Home. Two narrow cases can still show the old text: the end did not arrive before the force-stop, or the app was killed mid-game and reopened within the grace. A proper fix would be on the server: in GameRoom/FriendsRoom.onJoin, let the same account take over a held seat (release its allowReconnection), or answer 'roomClosed' when the phase is 'over'. That needs a deploy, so it is left for the main session to decide.

Item 1 also touches the 1st bug of interference-picker-grid-small only by its taskId; the 360dp opponent-card overflow (1st bug) was not in my scope.

issues.problem: The 'יעד' chip that shows only '…' is probably not fixed. The fixer could not reproduce it and assumed it came from the card hanging off-screen, but the chip's width does not depend on the card's position.
issues.evidence: TargetFrame.tsx: chipWrap is absolute with start:0/end:0 over the frame and alignItems:'center'. The chip has no width of its own; its width comes from measuring the text, which is <Text numberOfLines={1}> in Rubik 12/700, chipPaddingX 8. Where the card sits horizontally cannot change that measured width. The phone runs at density 540, which is 3.375 px per dp, a fractional scale. On Android, a numberOfLines=1 text inside a shrink-wrapped box at that kind of scale is a classic cause of rounding-down truncation to '…'. No test covers the chip text, and the report says 'could not reproduce in Jest'.
issues.suggestion: Treat it as open until the phone confirms it. Defensive fix: give the chip text a minWidth or a 1–2 dp width slack, or drop numberOfLines on this one short word (the chip already has a fixed height). Add a deviceCheck at density 540 with the card not cut off.

issues.problem: The friends-room 'server error' is only partly fixed. The client still maps the server's 'alreadyInRoom' to 'internal' ('משהו השתבש בשרת'). Two flows can still show that text instead of 'החדר נסגר.' or going Home: a force-stop before the 'over' state reached the phone, and a kill during the game followed by a relaunch within the held-seat window. The brief asked for 'החדר נסגר.' or Home directly.
issues.evidence: friendsDevice.ts now returns null only when session.hasGame && getView().status === 'over' on this phone. Server GameRoom.ts:430-431 refuses 'alreadyInRoom' whenever seat.sessionId !== null, which includes the time it holds the seat with allowReconnection, during the game and after the end. friendsProblemOf still maps alreadyInRoom to 'internal'. The fixer's own notes list both cases as remaining. Note also remoteGameHost.ts:1371, which says the rejoin route 'lets go' of an earlier connection; onJoin contradicts that.
issues.suggestion: Client-side, with no deploy: when the resume join gets 'alreadyInRoom', retry with backoff until the hold ends, as the ranked by-code path already does ('not noticed yet: try again'). If it then gets roomClosed or notFound, show 'החדר נסגר.' or go Home. Never map it to 'internal' on a resume. Or decide the server change (the same account takes over the held seat) with the main session.

issues.problem: Item 2a, the ~250 ms empty screen between GO! and the board, is not fixed (status partial, no code change). The intermittent blank still ships in the next APK.

issues.problem: After a return from the background, the abandonment countdown is hidden for the whole first reconnect attempt, and one attempt can last up to attemptTimeoutMs (5 s), or longer for a friends rejoin. If the player was away about 20–24 s and the network is really gone, they can be abandoned without ever seeing the countdown that spec §16.2 asks for.
issues.evidence: connectionModel.ts: `if (status.cause === 'background' && attempt === 1) return self('lost', attempt, null)`. remoteGameHost.ts comeBack() keeps attempt=1 for the whole tryOnce(), and attemptTimeoutMs is 5000 (line 283). The grace ends 25 s after lostAt, which the phone already knows (graceEndsAt).
issues.suggestion: Hide the countdown only for a short window after the app is back in front (for example ~1.5 s), or only while graceEndsAt − now is more than the attempt timeout. Show it right away when little time is left. Add a test: cause 'background', attempt 1, and 3 s of grace left should show the countdown.

issues.problem: For about 1 s after a return from the background, the lock card 'הלוח נעול עד שתחזור' ('locked until you return') still shows to a player who is already back. The brief listed it as part of the symptom ('show only the reconnecting state').
issues.evidence: The report says: 'The lock card still shows during that roughly 1 s lost state'. i18n he/game.json:93 lockedTitle = 'הלוח נעול עד שתחזור'.
issues.suggestion: Acceptable if Moshe agrees. Otherwise, while cause is 'background' on attempt 1, skip the lock card and show just the banner, or a neutral 'מתחבר מחדש…' title. No new key is needed if an existing reconnecting string is reused.

issues.problem: When a match falls through after the VS and the search comes back within ~4.2 s, the same SearchView instance is reused instead of a new one. Its 'rangeLine' state (the range it announced once) is kept, so TalkBack reads 'requeued' together with the old range rather than the current one. Before this change the search was mounted fresh, so the line was computed again.
issues.evidence: MatchScreen.tsx: the search case now renders <View key='pregame'><Layer key='search'>, the same keys as the outgoing layer in the pre-game cases. SearchView.tsx:63-66 sets rangeLine once and resets it only when m.alone. Line 73 builds the announcement as joinSentences([m.requeued && requeued, line]).

issues.problem: The sfx first-play fix is checked only against a fake that was written from the same hypothesis, so the Jest tests can't refute it. The theory is credible: media3's DefaultAudioSink keeps advancing its estimated play position after stop(), even on a track that never started, and ExoPlayer skips a seek to the current position while READY. Still, only the phone can confirm it.
issues.evidence: sfxFirstPlay.test.ts models 'idle player counts its clip as played' and 'same-ms seek skipped'. The two native calls go out separately: seekTo is an AsyncFunction runOnQueue(MAIN), play is a Function with runOnMain. Playable.kt seekTo((0.001*1000L).toLong()) = 1 ms, so the seek is real. The full mobile suite passes (409 suites, 6506 tests); tsc, eslint and i18n:check are clean.

items.id: 1 (MAJOR) pregame-found-countdown-reduced: in the first ranked game the matchFound chime, the '3' beat and the GO sound don't play
items.rootCause: Unchanged from the first report; the reviewer agrees it is credible. The cause is in sfx's first play of a player made ahead of time on Android. In dumpsys, the warm-up's players open their AudioTrack the moment they are made. While paused, media3 hands the short clip to the track and ends it, so after a few idle seconds the player counts the clip as played. sfx.play() then does seekTo(0)+play(). seekTo(0) on a READY player already at 0 ms is skipped by ExoPlayer (same position), so play() ends at once with no sound. The second play seeks back from ENDED, which is a real seek, so it plays. That gives 3 starts in game 1 against 5 in later games. Reviewer's low note: the Jest stand-in is written from this same hypothesis, so only the phone can confirm it. That is correct and accepted. The deviceCheck below is the real verification.
items.fix: apps/mobile/src/services/sfx.ts (unchanged this round): each player's first play seeks to FIRST_PLAY_AT_S = 0.001 s instead of 0. Players already played are tracked in a WeakSet. A seek to 1 ms is a real seek (Playable.kt rounds 0.001*1000 to 1 ms), so the track is flushed and rebuilt. Every later play seeks to 0 as before. No change to the warm-up, preloading or GO!→board timing.

New apps/mobile/src/screens/match/GoCover.tsx. The game screen now opens on GO! itself, so the moment between GO! and the board is never empty.

items.rootCause: (1) Cards cut off: at the largest display zoom the A16 is 320 dp wide (1080 px at density 540; the tester's '360x780' is a mix-up). Each 2-player card had a fixed width of 159 (size.playerCard.width), and DuelHud put both in a 288-dp row (320 minus the 16-dp gutters). 2 x 159 = 318, so the row overflowed by 30 dp. With RTL space-between, my card stayed at the right edge and the opponent's card started about 14 dp (48 px) off the left edge, which matches the reported bounds. That cut off its avatar, its score '0' and 'חושב…'. (2) The 'יעד' chip (reviewer's point, now confirmed from the QA screenshot qa-shots/RF8Y60PP2XZ-interference-picker-grid-small-2.png): the chip shows 'י…', the first letter plus an ellipsis. So the word was ellipsised because its drawn width came out a hair under its measured width. In TargetFrame.tsx the chip shrink-wraps a numberOfLines={1} Text. At density 3.375 the text's width goes from px to dp and back to px with pixel rounding, and Android's ellipsis then cuts the word. That rounding depends on the absolute x position, so whether it happens is luck of the position (the off-screen card made it more likely). Fixing the card does not guarantee the chip is fixed, as the reviewer said.
items.fix: (1) Unchanged from the first pass. New pure helper duelCardWidth(rowWidth) in components/player/metrics.ts: min(159, floor((row - 8) / 2)). PlayerCard takes an optional `width` prop. DuelHud measures its row with onLayout (starting from the window width minus the gutters) and gives the width to both cards. At 360 dp and up nothing changes (159). At 320 each card is 140. Score Teko 64 and name Rubik 16 are not shrunk. reactions/model defaultCardRect uses the same width. (2) New in this pass: TargetFrame's chip is now sized by a hidden copy of the word (opacity 0, aria-hidden, importantForAccessibility no-hide-descendants). The visible word sits over it in an absolute box, centred, that is metrics.targetFrame.chipSlack = 2 dp wider on each side than the measured word (start/end = chipPaddingX - chipSlack = 6). So the drawn width is always about 4 dp more than the measured width, and rounding can no longer trigger the ellipsis, in any language. The chip still looks the same: height 20, padding 8, Rubik 700 12. The word is still read once. Note added in components.md §3.4. Three existing tests that looked for the text 'יעד' with includeHiddenElements (they would now find two copies) now check the label by testID: sections.test, ArsenalOverlay.test and GameScreenGroup.test.
items.test: (1) apps/mobile/src/screens/game/__tests__/DuelHud.test.tsx: duelCardWidth fits two cards plus the gap at every width from 320 to 430, gives 159 at 360/390 and 140 at 320. DuelHud renders at 320 and 360 dp with equal cards that fit the row, score and name stay 64/16, and the cards follow the measured layout. Fails on the old code. (2) New case in apps/mobile/src/components/player/__tests__/PlayerCard.test.tsx, 'the "יעד" chip draws its word wider than measured…'. It checks a hidden sizer (opacity 0, aria-hidden) with 'יעד'. It checks the visible label (numberOfLines 1, centred) in an absolute box with start/end 6 inside a chip with padding 8, so there is 2 dp of slack each side. It checks that only one 'יעד' is accessible. It fails on the old code, which has no sizer and no slack. Runs: components/player, components/dev and screens/game (65 suites, 1094 tests) plus src/__tests__ (1191 tests) all pass. The first parallel run had timeouts in some e2e suites while other agents were running. Those passed on a rerun, and the affected suites passed (75/75). tsc -p apps/mobile shows no errors. eslint and prettier are clean on the changed files. No i18n keys were added.

rework.notes: The reviewer was right about the 'יעד' chip. The QA screenshot (old scratchpad qa-shots/RF8Y60PP2XZ-interference-picker-grid-small-2.png) shows 'י…', which means the word was ellipsised because it was a few pixels short of room. It is not a clipping side effect. This is now fixed without depending on Android internals: a hidden copy of the word sizes the chip, and the visible word gets 2 dp of extra room on each side. The tests that searched hidden elements for the text 'יעד' would now find two matches. I changed the three that did (sections.test, ArsenalOverlay.test and GameScreenGroup.test) to use testID 'target-chip-label'; these are one-line edits. The A16 at density 540 is 320 dp wide, not 360, so the card fix is checked at 320 and 360. At 320 each card is 140 dp, and the score and name are not shrunk. In en/ar/ru/tr the word 'הפרעה' on the button may end in '…' only at this extreme zoom, and a 3-digit score with its +delta may briefly overflow, which is rare. I used no adb, build, install, git stash or commit, and added no i18n keys.

items.rootCause: When the app goes to the background during an online game, RemoteGameHost closes the socket on purpose (ReconnectInfo.cause 'background') and reconnects when the app comes back. connectionStatusOf dropped `cause`, so connectionModel handled the return like a network drop. It built Self-Reconnecting 'lost' with the abandonment deadline: after 15 s away, secondsLeft = 10 (10 s soft phase + 15 s grace). For about 1 s, a player who was already back saw 'יש לך עוד 10 שניות לחזור · לפני שהמשחק ייחשב כנטישה' and the lock card 'הלוח נעול עד שתחזור'.
items.fix: connectionStatus.ts passes `cause` through on the 'reconnecting' status, as a new optional ConnectionStatus field. connectionModel.ts: a reconnect with cause 'background', on its first attempt, while more than RETURN_QUIET_MS (6 s) of grace is left, gives self('lost', attempt, null) plus `returning: true`. That means no secondsLeft or remainingMs, so the countdown card is hidden. This answers review low #2. The rule is checked against `now` on every tick, so the countdown appears as soon as 6 s or less are left, even inside the first try. If the try fails (attempt 2), the countdown comes back. A drop while the app is in the foreground keeps the countdown from the first try, as spec §16.2 says. For review low #3, SelfReconnecting.tsx LockCard says 'מסנכרן…' / 'המשחק נשמר בשרת וממשיך מאותה נקודה' when `returning`, not 'הלוח נעול עד שתחזור' / 'כשהחיבור יחזור נסנכרן:'. These are existing keys; nothing new was added. The banner 'החיבור שלך אבד · מתחבר מחדש… · ניסיון 1' stays as the reconnecting state.

items.rootCause: 2nd bug: the friends room after a surrender. (a) currentFriendsRoomCode() kept reporting the room while the session stayed connected on the results screen, so the next launch went to /room/[code]?resume=1. (b) The HTTP route POST /v1/rooms/join gives the player a ticket for their own seat. But GameRoom.onJoin refuses it with 'alreadyInRoom' (Colyseus close 4002) while the server still holds that seat for the dead connection. It holds it after the end until closeAt (closeAfterGameMs 60 s), and mid-game until the grace runs out. RemoteGameHost.enterFriends treated that refusal as final, and friendsProblemOf maps 'alreadyInRoom' to 'internal', so the screen said 'משהו השתבש בשרת. נסה שוב בעוד רגע.'. By the time of 'נסה שוב' the room had closed: 'החדר נסגר.'.
items.fix: (a) As before, friendsDevice.ts currentFriendsRoomCode() returns null once the session's game is over, so a finished room is forgotten and the next launch stays on Home. (b) New for the review's medium issue, client-side only, no deploy: remoteGameHost.ts enterFriends now goes through takeFriendsSeat(). A refusal with 'alreadyInRoom' is 'my seat is still held for an earlier connection of mine', not a server failure. It waits and tries again with a fresh reservation from the route each time (the first one is single use), with waits of 3, 6, 12 and 20 s (the last repeats), for at most friendsHeldSeatWaitMs = 75 s. That makes at most 5 extra POST /v1/rooms/join calls, well under the 20 per 10 minutes per account. Meanwhile the room screen stays in 'connecting'. When the hold ends, the room takes the player back. If the room closed, the route says roomClosed or notFound, and the screen shows 'החדר נסגר.' directly. Leaving the screen (close()) wakes the wait and stops the tries. Both are new options in RemoteHostOptions. Ranked reconnects already retried 'alreadyInRoom' and are unchanged.
items.test: friendsDevice.test.ts: 'past its game … no room to come back to at the next start'. friendsHost.test.ts, 4 new tests. 1) 'my seat still held … waits the hold out, then takes it': tries at 0/3/9 s (reserved, rejoin+reserved, rejoin+reserved), still 'connecting', then gets in when the hold lapses. 2) 'the room closed while my seat was held: … roomClosed, never a server failure': error roomClosed, and friendsProblemOf gives 'roomClosed'. 3) Gives up after friendsHeldSeatWaitMs with at most 5 rejoins. 4) Leaving while waiting makes no more tries. With the old enterFriends temporarily put back, tests 1 and 2 failed; the fix was then restored.
items.deviceCheck: Two phones, both signed in. Phone 1: 'צור חדר'. Phone 2 joins with the code. Start a 2-player game. A) Surrender on one phone and wait until both phones are on the results screen. Force-stop phone 1 and launch it again. Expected: it opens on Home, never 'משהו השתבש בשרת'. Repeat with the other phone surrendering. B) Start a new room and game. In the middle of the game, force-stop phone 1 and launch it again at once. Expected: 'חדר עם חברים' in the connecting state for up to about 20–40 s, then either back in the game/result or 'החדר נסגר.'. Never 'משהו השתבש בשרת. נסה שוב בעוד רגע.'. C) Surrender on phone 2, and force-stop phone 1 within a second of the surrender, before its results screen shows. Launch it again. Expected: connecting for up to about 60 s, then the result or 'החדר נסגר.', not the server error. Control: in the lobby before the start, force-stop phone 1 and launch it again: it goes straight back to the same room.

items.rootCause: LicensesScreen's LTR style was only { writingDirection: 'ltr', textAlign: 'left' }. Android ignores writingDirection. In RN 0.86 Android, under forceRTL the paragraph direction comes from the layout direction, so English text set to textAlign 'left' landed on the right. The flexDirection 'row' package rows and the license toggle rows also took the RTL order.
items.fix: The LTR style also sets the layout `direction: 'ltr'`, the same pattern the board and keypad use. This applies to names, versions, licence ids, copyright lines and the full OFL/MIT bodies. The package row and its name/version line get direction 'ltr', so the name is on the left with the version after it. New for review low #4: the Expandable toggle row ('SIL Open Font License 1.1', 'MIT') also gets direction 'ltr', so the title is on the left and the chevron on the right, like the package rows. Its accessibilityLabel (licenses.show/hide) did not change. The Hebrew headings, intro and hint keep the RTL layout.
items.test: LicensesScreen.test.tsx: 'keeps the English texts on the left in the Hebrew layout…'. It checks LTR direction, writingDirection and textAlign on package names, versions, copyright lines, the font copyright and the opened OFL/MIT bodies. Removing only the toggle's direction makes the test fail. The earlier assertions fail on the old code.

Checks: 105 related suites run (net, screens/game, legal, friends, game, auth, dev, ranked e2e): 104 pass, 1592 tests. The one failing suite, apps/mobile/src/screens/game/__tests__/gameRoute.test.tsx, fails to load: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading colors)' at src/theme/transitions.ts:19, imported through src/screens/match/GoCover.tsx from app/game.tsx. app/game.tsx was changed this round by another agent (git diff refs/qa/snap-loop4), and none of my files are involved. The agent working on app/game.tsx / GoCover needs to look at it, probably a missing DarkTheme mock in that test. `npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit`: clean. ESLint: clean on all 12 changed files. Prettier was run on them. No i18n keys added. No server changes, adb, builds, deploys or commits.

Remaining, for the main session: the root cause on the server is that GameRoom.onJoin (GameRoom.ts:430) refuses a same-account join while it holds that account's dropped seat. This contradicts remoteGameHost.ts:1371's comment that the route 'lets go' of an earlier connection. Proper server fix: in onJoin, when seat.sessionId is a held (dropped) session, release its allowReconnection deferred (keep a sessionId→reject map, under a name other than FriendsRoom's private `holds`) and give the seat to the new client. The killed-mid-game player would then get back in at once instead of waiting until the hold lapses. That wait currently ends at the abandonment, so mid-game the client retry gives a clean message but not a saved game. The server fix needs a deploy, so I left it alone. If the hold somehow outlasts the 75 s client window, friendsProblemOf still maps 'alreadyInRoom' to 'internal' as a last resort; I did not change that mapping, since friends.test.ts:524 pins it.
